commit_reviews.summary: The refactor heads in a sound direction (extracting dev-server/markdown/template behind a Plugin interface) but the code is minified into unreadable one-liners, placed in a non-standard module location, and mismatches the engine's plugin contract.

compounding_issues: Session 1's hardcoded pageDocument/indexDocument HTML generation coexisted with the new template system added in Session 2, leaving two competing render paths until the Session 4 plugin refactor unified them under TemplatePlugin
Session 2 introduced a bespoke regex-based Handlebars/EJS renderer that was carried verbatim into plugins/template.ts in Session 4 — a hand-maintained template engine with no dependency backing

Session 3's dev server was built as a full module (src/serve.ts) and then had to be reworked into a plugin in Session 4, retaining a serve.ts compat wrapper alongside the plugin, adding a thin redundant layer
The incremental cache manifest written into outputDir (.ssg-cache.json) couples cache state with build artifacts, requiring the --clean flag as a workaround for stale cache issues
key_decisions: Session 2: frontmatter-driven template/layout/partial selection with a zero-dependency Handlebars/EJS-compatible renderer instead of adding template library dependencies
Session 3: integrated dev server using chokidar file watching + WebSocket live-reload with path-traversal-safe static serving
Session 4: plugin architecture with lifecycle hooks (onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd) and ssg.config.ts loader, extracting markdown, template, and dev-server into plugins/
Session 5: incremental build manifest with SHA256 source/template hashing, stale-output removal, and BuildStats surfaced through the CLI
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved monotonically across all five sessions. Session 1 established a clean, well-tested markdown-to-HTML core; Session 2 cleanly layered template/layout/partial support onto it without breaking the base; Session 3 integrated a polished dev-server with live reload and defensive path handling; Session 4 was the riskiest step — a large plugin extraction that removed ~400 lines while preserving external API behavior and all tests (4 tests held green through the refactor); Session 5 added genuinely valuable cross-cutting engineering — incremental caching, cache invalidation, and build stats — expanding tests to 6 and deepening the plugin pipeline rather than regressing it. Test coverage grew steadily (2→6 tests) and no session regressed previously shipped behavior.
story_review.summary: A textbook greenfield→feature→integration→refactor→cross-cutting progression that stayed coherent, kept tests green through a major refactor, and delivered steadily improving code quality.
